What can change the investment view
The base case needs FY27 H2 sales of INR1,231.3 crore, around 20.1% growth over H2 FY26, and H2 company EBITDA
of INR232.6 crore. Announcements and revenue visibility alone do not demonstrate this outcome. A second quarter of
weak sequential revenue or EBITDA below 18% would warrant a lower recovery path.
AI-enabled learning creates demand for coaching, simulation and workflow integration. It can also reduce
content-development hours and vendor pricing. The disclosed 17% revenue contribution measures product mix, not
incremental AI revenue or profit. Evidence of margins and renewals is needed before assigning a software multiple.
The top 10 clients generate 48% of revenue. A delayed programme at one large client can outweigh new-logo wins.
Corporate restructuring can stimulate outsourcing but also cut training volumes; neither impact is certain.
MST and SweetRush alter year-on-year comparability. Bluewater adds integration and cash commitments after the reported
balance-sheet date; purchase price is up to USD17.6 million over five years including earnouts. Outstanding options of
about 1.11 crore equal roughly 8% of September issued shares; this is gross option overhang, not immediate diluted shares.
Watch the next Q3/Q4 results for new-contract revenue, a return toward 19-20% EBITDA margins, DSO/cash conversion
and Bluewater integration. No exact result date was verified. The Overweight case weakens if FY28 EPS cannot approach
INR20 or if earnings remain dependent on valuation reversals and acquisition accounting.
Catalysts are operating conditions to monitor, not guaranteed outcomes. Currency, tax, competition and small-cap liquidity add risk.
